Class StepProcessor

java.lang.Object
javax.annotation.processing.AbstractProcessor
be.imgn.gaia.processing.StepProcessor
All Implemented Interfaces:
Processor
public abstract class StepProcessor extends AbstractProcessor
An annotation processor made of Steps, which takes care of processing rounds. 
public final class MapperProcessor extends StepProcessor {
    protected List<Step> steps(ProcessingContext context) {
        return List.of(new MapperStep(context));
    }
}

Each round, each step gets the elements annotated with its annotations, or with annotations that its meta-annotations annotate, grouped by annotation. An element whose signature still has a type javac could not resolve, typically one another processor has yet to generate, is held back until a later round resolves it. So is an element a step gives back. An element still held back after the last round is reported as an error, with the type that blocked it. Then each step finishes, and the processor writes the service files its steps registered with ProcessingContext.services(), whatever errors were reported.

A ProcessingException that escapes a step is reported as an error, at the place it names, and the processor goes on with the next step: the elements of that step in that round are done, none is given back to it. To go on with the next element instead, a step processes each with ProcessingContext.forEach(Iterable, java.util.function.Consumer). The same goes for Step.processingOver(). Any other exception propagates: javac stops and reports it, with its stack trace, as a crash of the processor.

The processor supports the annotations of its steps, or all annotations if a step has meta-annotations, and the latest source version. It never claims the annotations, so other processors see them too.

Every step processor accepts the boolean option gaia.debug, as -Agaia.debug or -Agaia.debug=true, which turns on its debug output: javac notes, each starting with the simple name of the processor. Each round, one note per step that had work tells which elements it got, how many it gave back, how many were held back with an unresolved type, how many errors it reported through the diagnostics of the context, and how long it took. One note per round sums its steps up. In the last round, a step only has a note if its Step.processingOver() reported errors; its time counts in the totals either way. After the last round, one note per step and one for the processor give the totals over all rounds. A step is named by its name, by default the simple name of its class, numbered with # if several steps have the same. The rounds are those the processor takes part in.
